chunks: Muhammad narrated from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the earth, upon what is it? He said: 'It is upon a whale.' I said: 'So the whale, upon what is it?' He said: 'Upon the water.' I said: 'So the water, upon what is it?' He said: 'Upon a rock.' I said: 'So upon what is the rock?' He said: 'Upon the horn of a smooth bull.' I said: 'So upon what is the bull?' He said: 'Upon the earth/dust.' I said: 'So upon what is the earth?' He said: 'Far off! At that point, the knowledge of the scholars is exhausted/strays.'
ai.seo_question: What is the earth resting upon according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This cosmological narrative from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia tradition of 'ta'wil' (interpretive layering), where the physical description serves as a metaphor for the hierarchical structure of existence rather than a literal scientific claim. The Imam’s concluding remark, 'there knowledge strays,' highlights the epistemological limit of human reason when confronting the divine mystery of creation, a concept central to Usuli scholarship. It emphasizes that while scholars can map the visible world, the ultimate foundation remains within the realm of divine knowledge beyond full human comprehension.
